answer: Anchor each agent identity to a dye trace through a karst cave system. The agent buys one batch of fluorescent pigment, releases it at a registered sinkhole, and hydrology stations watch for it in glacier-fed springs downstream. Identity activates only after the pigment is confirmed at two separate outlets, days apart, proving the claim survived real underground transit. One fake identity costs $400 in dye and field work plus weeks of waiting; a thousand sybils cost $400,000 and months of field trips. Like a glacier grinding a valley, the process moves one way and cannot be rushed.
